arxiv-1910-06512.title: Design- and Model-Based Approaches to Small-Area Estimation in a Low and Middle Income Country Context: Comparisons and Recommendations
arxiv-1910-06512.creator: John Paige, Geir-Arne Fuglstad, Andrea Riebler, Jon Wakefield
arxiv-1910-06512.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by John Paige, Geir-Arne Fuglstad, Andrea Riebler, Jon Wakefield. The need for rigorous and timely health and demographic summaries has provided the impetus for an explosion in geographic studies, with a common approach being the production of pixel-level maps, particularly in low and middle income countries. In this context, household surveys are a major source of data, usually with a two-stage cluster design with stratification by region and urbanicity.

arxiv-2107-06827.title: Localization effects due to a random magnetic field on heat transport in a harmonic chain
arxiv-2107-06827.creator: Gaëtan Cane, Junaid Majeed Bhat, Abhishek Dhar, Cédric Bernardin
arxiv-2107-06827.description: Abstract We consider a harmonic chain of N N oscillators in the presence of a disordered magnetic field. The ends of the chain are connected to heat baths and we study the effects of the magnetic field randomness on heat transport. The disorder, in general, causes localization of the normal modes due to which a system becomes insulating.

arxiv-2212-01805.title: Decoupling inequality for paraboloid under shell type restriction and its application to the periodic Zakharov system
arxiv-2212-01805.creator: Shinya Kinoshita, Shohei Nakamura, Akansha Sanwal
arxiv-2212-01805.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shinya Kinoshita, Shohei Nakamura, Akansha Sanwal. In this paper, we establish local well-posedness for the Zakharov system on 𝕋 d \mathbb{T}^{d} , d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 in a low regularity setting. Our result improves the work of Kishimoto [ 47 ] . Moreover, the result is sharp up to ε \varepsilon -loss of regularity when d = 3 d=3 and d ≥ 5 d\geq 5 as long as one utilizes the iteration argument.

arxiv-2408-02920.title: Analysis of Architecture Options for Foundation-model-based Agents: A Taxonomy and Decision Model
arxiv-2408-02920.creator: Jingwen Zhou, Qinghua Lu, Jieshan Chen, Liming Zhu, Xiwei Xu, Zhenchang Xing, Stefan Harrer
arxiv-2408-02920.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of foundation models has led to a new generation of AI-based agents. While mature frameworks exist, the system-level architectural decision-making is still often ad-hoc, as architects lack a systematic, evidence-based framework for navigating the complex landscape of architectural options and their resulting trade-offs.

arxiv-2408-11270.title: Disordered Parity Anomalous Semimetal
arxiv-2408-11270.creator: Shi-Hao Bi, Bo Fu, Shun-Qing Shen
arxiv-2408-11270.description: Abstract The parity anomalous semimetal is a topological state of matter characterized by its semi-metallic nature and a quantum Hall conductance of one-half e 2 / h e^{2}/h ( e e is the elementary charge and h h is the Planck constant).

arxiv-2511-19963.title: MambaEye: A Size-Agnostic Visual Encoder with Causal Sequential Processing
arxiv-2511-19963.creator: Changho Choi, Minho Kim, Jinkyu Kim
arxiv-2511-19963.description: Abstract Despite decades of progress, a truly input-size agnostic visual encoder—a fundamental characteristic of human vision—has remained elusive. We address this limitation by proposing MambaEye , a novel, causal sequential encoder that leverages the low complexity and causal-process based pure Mamba2 backbone.

pmc-11388005.title: Two serial filters control P2X7 cation selectivity, Ser342 in the central pore and lateral acidic residues at the cytoplasmic interface
pmc-11388005.creator: Fritz Markwardt, Eike Christian Schön, Mihaela Raycheva, Aparna Malisetty, Sanaria Hawro Yakoob, Malte Berthold, Günther Schmalzing, Ivet Bahar
pmc-11388005.description: The human P2X7 receptor (hP2X7R) is a homotrimeric cell surface receptor gated by extracellular ATP4− with two transmembrane helices per subunit, TM1 and TM2. A ring of three S342 residues, one from each pore-forming TM2 helix, located halfway across the membrane bilayer, functions to close and open the gate in the apo and ATP4−-bound open states, respectively.

pmc-11674041.title: Automatic Segmentation of Metastatic Livers by Means of U-Net-Based Procedures
pmc-11674041.creator: Camilla Tiraboschi, Federica Parenti, Fabio Sangalli, Andrea Resovi, Dorina Belotti, Ettore Lanzarone
pmc-11674041.description: Simple SummaryIn this work, we developed three neural networks based on the U-net architecture to automatically segment the healthy liver area, the metastatic liver area, and liver metastases in micro-CT images of mice with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and liver metastases. The best network for each task was then identified by cross-validation.

pmc-12719729.title: Identification of Cathepsin L as the Molecular Target of Hydroxychloroquine With Chemical Proteomics
pmc-12719729.creator: Jin Shang, Bingjie Hu, Karen Ka-Yan Kung, Jiajun Jiang, Qi Zhang, Man-Kin Wong, Hin Chu, Qian Zhao
pmc-12719729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) and chloroquine have been utilized as antimalarial drugs for decades. Recently, these compounds were reported to inhibit various viruses utilizing the endosomal entry pathway. However, their direct molecular targets in host cells remain elusive. In this study, we developed a clickable photo-crosslinking probe in combination with proteomic approaches to identified cathepsin L (CTSL) as the binding target of HCQ. Extensive biochemical and in silico analyses were conducted to validate the HCQ–CTSL interactions.

pmc-13035709.title: The spatial and environmental distribution of the global eddy covariance tower network
pmc-13035709.creator: Paul C. Stoy, Housen Chu, Emma Dahl, Daniela S. Cala, Victoria Shveytser, Susanne Wiesner, Ankur R. Desai, Kimberly A. Novick
pmc-13035709.description: Eddy covariance has revolutionized our understanding of ecosystem-atmosphere interactions. Multiple studies have characterized the climate space occupied by flux tower networks, but none to our knowledge have characterized if eddy covariance sites represent the global distribution of soil characteristics that are critical for determining ecosystem function or studied the distances between towers to apply ‘paired’ tower studies.

pmc-13157632.title: Treponemal Endovasculitis leading to branch artery occlusion: a rare manifestation of ocular syphilis
pmc-13157632.creator: Kakarla V Chalam, Lourdes Ceja, Anny M S Cheng
pmc-13157632.description: Ocular syphilis, a re-emerging cause of uveitis, commonly features retinal vasculitis, but branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO) is a rare, irreversible damaging complication. We present a 47-year-old woman with bilateral syphilitic panuveitis, retinal vasculitis and an inferior BRAO, emphasising the diagnostic value of multimodal imaging.

pmc-13203346.title: Sensory Neuroimmunology: Bidirectional Neuro-Immune Circuits Governing Pain, Itch, Inflammation, and Host Defense at Barrier Surfaces
pmc-13203346.creator: Reza Mosaddeghi-Heris, Nasrin Forghani, Negin Safari Dehnavi, Maryam Saberivand, Amir Tahavvori, Sohrab Azin, Niloofar Taheri, Paolo Martelletti
pmc-13203346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummarySensory neurons in the skin, lung, and gut directly sense immune signals and actively shape local inflammation, pain, itch, and host defense. Immune cells also alter neuronal excitability through cytokines and alarmins, forming bidirectional circuits at barrier tissues. This review organizes recent evidence into a circuit-based framework across organs and discusses how targeting neuronal components may relieve disease symptoms while affecting protective immune responses.
